children: Shares of New India Assurance Company Ltd (NIACL) and IFCI Ltd surged up to 11 percent in Wednesday's trading session amid buzz that subscription to the National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO could begin this month.
Unconfirmed reports said the IPO could be launched this month, triggering buying interest in stocks of companies that hold a stake in the NSE.
Shares of IFCI Ltd surged 11 percent to a high of Rs 96.66 per share on the NSE.
IFCI, a public sector non-banking financial company (NBFC), holds a 52 percent stake in Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL), which in turn owns a 4.4 percent stake in the NSE.
Shares of New India Assurance Company rose 6.74 percent to Rs 198.30 per share.
New India Assurance Company holds a 1.42 percent stake in the NSE.

Meanwhile, State Bank of India (SBI) and its subsidiary SBI Capital Markets Ltd plan to dilute up to 1 percent stake in the NSE through the exchange's proposed Rs 30,000-crore initial public offering (IPO).
SBI is participating in the NSE IPO and will dilute a 0.65 percent stake in the exchange, SBI Chairman C S Setty told PTI in an interview.
SBI currently holds a 3.23 percent stake in the NSE, while SBI Capital Markets owns 4.33 percent.
NSE has marketed its shares at Rs 2,000-2,100 per share during meetings with potential investors, Bloomberg reported.

At the top of the marketed range, NSE would rank sixth in market value among global exchange operators, narrowly behind London Stock Exchange Group Plc and ahead of Nasdaq Inc. CME Group Inc. and Intercontinental Exchange Inc. are currently the top two, with market values of about USD 97 billion and USD 86.9 billion, respectively.

At a USD 55 billion valuation, NSE's sale of a 6 percent stake could raise about Rs 31,500 crore, surpassing the Rs 27,870 crore raised by Hyundai Motor Co's Indian unit in 2024, the country's largest IPO to date.
National Stock Exchange of India Ltd, the operator of the world's largest derivatives exchange by trading volume, is seeking a valuation of as much as Rs 5.26 lakh crore in its planned IPO.
Reports have suggested that the NSE could trade on its own exchange via the "permitted to trade" category after listing on the BSE.

title: NSE IPO soon? NIACL, IFCI shares jump up to 11% on buzz over issue launch
